svg.text: Iskar midships (1,200–3,900 m) at true scale · elevation and plan share each row · interior placement simplified
A · AS BUILT — cruisers lying flat
Two 280 m-tall dockyards in the keel. Everything above them stays intact.
Keel openings ~1.5 km² · bay volume ~0.54 km³ · stacked lanes launch in pairs
B · CRUISERS STANDING ON END — 20 shafts, nose down
Saves volume and shrinks the keel openings, but each shaft runs almost the full 840 m height.
wing stories and the decks between
Keel openings ~0.4 km² · shaft volume ~0.31 km³ · but the shafts pierce the Hangar Bay, the Frigate Deck and every district between.
A returning cruiser backs 720 m up a tube with ~5 m to spare each side.
C · FRIGATES STANDING ON END — 40 shafts in the keel spine
Height is no problem (310 m), and the whole Frigate Deck is freed. The only keel left to put them in is the spine.
Shaft volume ~0.04 km³ · frees the Frigate Deck (~0.08 km³) · but cuts a 520 m stretch out of the solid spine that carries the keel loads
between the two dockyards, and displaces the magazines kept there.
